title: Extract the duplicated router/guard mock harness out of 4 test/app/restore/*_test.dart files into one shared helper
rule: TQ-3 (shared pump/harness helper) / Fowler duplicated code
why: _MockStackRouter, _MockRestoreGuard, _StubAppRouter, and the _makeRouter()/_buildHarness() pattern (ProviderScope overrides for restoreStatusProvider, deviceRestoreServiceProvider, routerProvider, userDatabaseProvider, currentAccountIdProvider, selectedProfileIdProvider wrapped in a MaterialApp with the same localizationsDelegates list) are copy-pasted near-byte-identically across all 4 restore test files in this batch — confirmed via direct text comparison, not just naming. The project already has a `pumpApp` helper convention used elsewhere (test/e2e/journeys/*), and test/helpers/ has no equivalent for this restore-specific harness, so each new restore test file re-derives it from scratch. Concrete cost: a change to AppRouter's or RestoreGuard's interface (e.g. a new method the screen calls) requires editing the same stub in 4+ places; the next restore test file will likely paste a 5th copy, and any router-mocking bug fixed in one copy silently persists in the other three.
recommendation: Extract a shared test/app/restore/restore_test_harness.dart (or add to test/helpers/) exposing the mock classes, _makeRouter()/_makeAppRouter(), and a parameterized _buildHarness()/pumpApp()-style entry point; have all 4 files import it instead of redefining it.
acceptance_criteria: A single shared helper file defines _MockStackRouter/_MockRestoreGuard/_StubAppRouter and the harness builder.

The 4 files in this batch (device_restore_phase_l10n_test.dart, device_restore_screen_l1_test.dart, device_restore_screen_overflow_test.dart, sy2_device_restore_idle_blank_test.dart) import it instead of each defining their own copy; grep for 'class _MockStackRouter' across test/app/restore/ returns exactly one hit.

corrections: Minor overstatement: only 3 of 4 files (phase_l10n, screen_l1, sy2_idle_blank) share the literal _buildHarness() function — device_restore_screen_overflow_test.dart uses a structurally different _statusOverride() list instead. Doesn't change viability of the fix.
